truthAudit.Summary: Audited Run 2 against the supplied enhanced_calc.cpp truth set. Run 2 fully identified 13 of 20 true vulnerabilities, partially identified 2, and missed 5. It also overclaimed severity or CWE on several matched findings and included extra findings that are not credited by the supplied truth set.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Format string vulnerability in debug logging
Items.Notes: Previous answer explicitly reported printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) and stated active_format can be changed by set_runtime_log_format and config loading, matching the true runtime format-string vulnerability.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Signed integer overflow in factorial function
Items.Notes: Previous answer cited the factorial loop with result *= i and identified signed integer overflow for large inputs.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Use-after-free from memory pool cleanup before thread pool drains
Items.Notes: Previous answer cited scratch allocation, queued lambda reading scratch, stage_deferred_history_flush, and memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup while the thread pool was still alive.
Previous answer cited validator_cmd plus config_file and system(command.c_str()) in validate_config, matching the true config validation command injection.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Inverted strcpy causes stack buffer overflow
Items.Notes: Previous answer reported the inverted length check and strcpy into input_buffer_ for expressions at or above the buffer size. It also separately reported the safe_string_copy null-terminator edge case.
Previous answer cited volatile long long value_, old_value read before locking, value_ = old_value + 1, and unlocked get(), matching the true counter race.
Previous answer cited login_attempts_ > 5, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE, and authenticated_ = true, matching the true authentication logic bomb.
Previous answer cited config_dir_ + filename in load_config and admin load constructing filename without path canonicalization.
Previous answer cited buffer_size_ = 256 and unbounded strcpy into expression_buffer_ in the expression parser.
Previous answer cited ADMIN_SECRET and SC_ENT_2025_AUTH, matching the true hardcoded credential finding.

Previous answer identified a low-entropy session token using uniform_int_distribution 1000 to 9999, but did not explicitly identify std::mt19937 as a weak PRNG or assign the true High severity and CWE-338 classification.
No previous finding addressed the thread-unsafe static std::tm cached_time cache or the localtime/cached_time race in logging.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Command injection in emergency audit logging
Items.Notes: Previous answer touched TEMP/TMPDIR and system in the emergency audit path, but framed it as command injection rather than insecure temporary file handling and did not explicitly identify supercalc_emergency.log in the quoted evidence.
No previous finding addressed persistent authentication state as the security issue, such as authenticated_, login_attempts_, and session_token_ persisting without proper session lifecycle controls.
No previous finding addressed unhandled exceptions from std::stod(tokens[3]) in handle_variable_command.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Memory pool block split underflow creates out-of-bounds block
Items.Notes: Previous answer cited previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES underflow and the resulting fragment pointing outside the original block.
No previous finding addressed unbounded recursion through parse_expression, parse_factor, and PAREN_OPEN handling.
Previous answer cited unsynchronized result_cache_ access in evaluate_cached despite cache_mutex_ and concurrent thread-pool enqueueing.
No previous finding addressed the TOCTOU pattern in config loading using std::filesystem::exists, sleep_for, and then std::ifstream.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Division by zero in route score calculation
Items.Notes: Previous answer cited 100 divided by static_cast<int>(token_length) in calculate_route_score and identified empty or leading-space input as a zero-length trigger.
